title: Victim-offender mediation (VOM) services
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) has a requirement to deliver post-sentence victim-offender mediation services to individuals impacted by serious crime (federally sentenced offences). The Contractor must provide services to victims residing in British Columbia and the Northern Territories (Yukon, Northwest Territories, & Nunavut), as well as to offenders who are incarcerated or on conditional release within these regions. This includes cross-regional cases where one participant is located within the region specified and the other is outside said region and supported by a mediator assigned to another region (Prairie, Ontario, Quebec, Atlantic). The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objective: To provide victim-offender mediation (VOM) services in accordance with the Victim-Offender Mediation Program (VOMP) model CSC has approved, based on the values and principles of restorative justice. The goal of delivering VOM services is to provide victims and offenders, in western Canada and the northern territories, the opportunity to communicate about and address the harms caused by the offence(s). The expected result is to prepare, facilitate, and assess safety throughout the restorative justice process between the participants and to meet their needs in areas of accountability, information sharing, increased understanding and empathy, healing, safety planning and the prevention of future harm. The Contractor must provide a minimum of two (2) qualified and professional victim-offender mediators to respond to all referrals requesting victim-offender mediation services involving offenders under CSC's jurisdiction. The mediators must collectively deliver approximately 3,500 hours of victim-offender mediation services annually to meet the following requirements: a. Deliver a combined minimum of 20 hours to a maximum of 80 hours per week of mediation services; b. Provide expertise, training and consultation on the Victim-Offender Mediation Program (VOMP) process model addressing serious crime with CSC’s Restorative Opportunities mediators, Restorative Justice Division, and CSC operational staff. c. Provide the level of expertise and mediation skills expected to complete victim-offender mediation processes, based on the VOMP process model, that include and are not limited to: i. Letter exchanges ii. Video exchanges iii. Shuttle mediation iv. Community conferencing v. Healing circles vi. Face-to-face meetings. 1.2 Tasks/Responsibilities: The Contractor must complete the following tasks that include, but are not limited to: 1. Forward all victim-offender mediation referrals received from CSC staff and contracted service providers working at the institutional and community level, from victims of crime, victim serving agencies, Parole Board Canada staff to the Restorative Justice Division at National Headquarters (NHQ) for initial review, creation of a case initiation form and Offender Management System (OMS) file creation in the Restorative Justice (RJ) Module. 2. Receive case referrals for victim-offender mediation services through CSC’s Restorative Justice Division, NHQ. 3. Assess all case referrals to determine their suitability for victim-offender mediation services. For cases deemed appropriate, the Contractor must prepare all participants for a victim-offender mediation process based on the participants needs and in accordance with VOMP process model. The contractor must begin with the participant that requested the service and only move on to the other participant if consent is given by the participant to proceed. 4. Perform ongoing assessments at each stage of the VOMP process and throughout service delivery to determine safety, security and confidentiality. 5. Maintain accurate and up to date records of all victim-offender mediation case activities by entering weekly updates in the RJ Module in OMS within 7 business days of the case activity taking place. 6. Participate in the annual Restorative Opportunities (RO) gathering and all other RO video conference calls, WebEx, MSTeams and Zoom meetings as requested by the Project Authority (PA). 1.3 Expected results: The Contractor must prepare, assess, and deliver post-sentence victim-offender mediation services addressing serious crime for voluntary victim and offender participants residing in British Columbia and the Northern Territories (Yukon, Northwest Territories, & Nunavut), as well as for cross-regional cases. The Contractor must provide Victims with the opportunity to tell the offender about the crime’s physical, emotional and financial impact on their lives, receive answers to lingering questions about the crime and the offender, and participate directly in developing options to address the participant’s needs and the harms caused by the crime(s). The offender is afforded opportunities to provide information, be held accountable, and to develop reparative plans and gain insight for personal growth. The Contractor must share information about the program and services provided and offer victim-offender mediation services through the Restorative Opportunities (RO) program. The purpose of CSC’s RO program is to assist individuals affected by serious crime by: a) Empowering them to address issues and concerns surrounding the crime and its consequences. b) Providing victims and offenders with a process that can lead to new insight about the offence, the harms caused, and actions that can be taken towards reparation and the prevention of future harms, thereby reducing levels of anxiety; and c) Addressing questions and concerns regarding the offender’s eventual release into the community. 1.4 Performance standards: 1.The following CSC laws, directives, guidelines and policies apply to the work: a. Corrections and Conditional Release Act, s.26.1(1) and (2) b. Commissioner's directive 785: Restorative opportunities and victim-offender mediation services c. Guidelines 785-1 : Restorative opportunities program protocols d. Canadian Victims Bill of Rights, s.6 e. Privacy Act f. Access to Information Act g. Witness Protection Program Act 2. The Contractor must complete all tasks and deliverables as per Commissioner’s Directive (CD) 785 Restorative Opportunities and Victim-Offender Mediation Services, as well as related protocols. 1.5 Deliverables: 1.5.1 The Contractor must provide the following deliverables to the Project Authority (PA): a. Accept and manage all case referrals, including a minimum of 25 newly referred cases per year, while continuing to work on all active cases carried over from previous years, as requested. b. Provide weekly updates in the OMS RJ Module for all active mediation files, including detailed documentation of all activities and any new and relevant information related to each file. c. Submit (1) one victim-offender mediation case study annually using the template and the consent form provided by the project Authority (PA). Deliverable Format 1. The Contractor must complete and provide all deliverable documents to the Project Authority (PA) using Microsoft Office software. 2. The Contractor must submit all deliverables in English; CSC will be responsible for any required translation. 3. The Contractor must complete ongoing updates the Restorative Justice (RJ) Module in OMS i

description: This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Joyceville Institution, Ontario Region. Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements. The Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements applies to this bid solicitation. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is open to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous businesses. All interested suppliers may participate. However, suppliers are to note that this requirement is subject to a preference for Indigenous suppliers and will be set-aside under the federal government Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB) if Canada receives two or more responsive bids from Indigenous businesses who meet the requirements of the PSIB. Indigenous businesses that have not already registered in the Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory should do so. Additional information on the Indigenous Business Directory is available at the following link: https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100033057/1610797769658#c3. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) has a requirement to replace the sidewalk between buildings JVJ25 & JVJ1 at Joyceville Institution. Deliverables: The Contractor must: a) Supply material, labour, and equipment to remove the existing sidewalk, and to install a new sidewalk between buildings JVJ25 to JVJ1. b) Remove and dispose of off-site the existing concrete sidewalk (approx. 2,000 ft2), including all associated debris. c) Excavate and prepare subgrade as required. d) Supply and install a compacted gravel sub-base suitable for sidewalk construction. e) Raise sub-base as necessary so that finished concrete surface is above adjacent sod/grade to prevent water pooling on new sidewalk. f) Install new concrete sidewalk with proper alignment and thickness. The concrete must be 25MPa sidewalk-grade concrete and must slope away from all buildings to ensure positive drainage. g) Provide and maintain temporary walkways and safe access routes where required during construction to ensure pedestrian safety. h) Restore disturbed areas adjacent to sidewalk upon completion of work. i) Comply with applicable codes, site standards, and safety regulations. j) Keep the surrounding area clean and safe throughout the duration of the project. k) Provide a complete project schedule ten (10) business days after award of contract for approval by the Project Authority. l) Provide the Project Authority with a final report for CSC review and sign-off upon completion. The report must detail all work completed and include photographs. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Construction Time: The Contractor must perform and complete the Work by January 31st, 2027. File Number: 21450-27-5533027 Contracting Authority: Robin Riha Telephone number: 613-328-9727 E-mail: robin.riha@csc-scc.gc.ca NOTE TO BIDDERS: Bidders can obtain the complete statement of work and evaluation criteria by downloading the solicitation document and associated documents from the Canada buys / tender opportunities website. The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French). After contract award, bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. Understand the federal procurement process; ? Learn about searching for opportunities; ? Find out how to bid on opportunities; ? Discover how to prepare to sell to the government. The full schedule of seminars can be found on the Procurement Assistance Canada website, under find an event (Procurement Assistance Canada: Find an event - Canada.ca).

title: RFSO - Civil/Marine Engineering Consulting Services - Ontario, Prairie & Northwest Territories Regions
description: 1. Requirement Overview and Scope Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) – Small Craft Harbours (SCH) Branch is inviting consulting firms with Marine Engineering expertise to submit proposals for Standing Offers. The selected consultants shall provide a range of services as identified in the Required Services section of this document for marine projects in the Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and Northwest Territories Regions, including but not limited to the following: ? Small Craft Harbour facilities ? Shore protection and breakwaters ? Dredging ? Timber cribwork ? Steel sheet pilework ? Timber or steel pilework & rock anchors ? Reinforced concrete support structures (e.g. pile caps, beams, fascia and retaining walls, wharf deck) ? Inspection, investigations and site assessments of existing structures (barricading, load capacity) ? Other engineering services (electrical, civil, geotechnical, etc.) 2. Mandatory Licensing and Evaluation Basis Offerors shall be licensed or eligible to be licensed to practice in the Province having Jurisdiction. If an Offeror is licensed to practice in only one of the specified jurisdictions, then that Offeror must be eligible and willing to be licensed in the jurisdiction in which they are not licensed. In general, the firm and its personnel will be evaluated on the basis of their demonstrated understanding of the scope of services, their approach and methodology to providing those services, the quality of their relevant experience in this area, as well as the cost of the provision of the services. 3. Standing Offer Structure and Duration It is DFO's intention to authorize up to five (5) Standing Offers per Region. Regions are defined as follows: I. Ontario Region - Ontario. II. Prairie & Northwest Territories Region - Manitoba; - Saskatchewan; - Alberta; and - Northwest Territories. The period for placing call-ups against the Standing Offer shall be for Five (5) years commencing from the start date identified on the Standing Offer. 4. Financial Value of the Standing Offers Individual call-ups will vary, up to a maximum of $750,000.00 (Applicable Taxes included). Offerors should note that there is no guarantee that the full or any amount of the Standing Offer will be called up; DFO will issue call-ups only when the specific services to be provided under the Standing Offer are needed. 5. Applicable Trade Agreements This procurement is subject to the provisions of the World Trade Organization - Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), the Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CColFTA), the Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPanFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), the Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), the Canada - United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA). 6. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement Applies No 7. Language of Work The language of work will be English or French. 8. Security Requirements There are no security requirements associated with this solicitation of offers or the Standing Offer; however, security requirements may be applicable at the time of issuance of call-ups. 9. Period of Standing Offer The period for making call-ups against the Standing Offer will be from the date of Standing Offer issuance to five(5) years later.

title: Propeller Wash and Clamshell Dredging, Fraser River, BC
description: Propeller Wash and Clamshell Dredging, Fraser River, BC Small Craft Harbours (SCH) requires propeller wash dredging and clamshell dredging services at the following four sites located on the Fraser River: 1. Kanaka Landing Small Craft Harbour is located on the north side of the Fraser River at the foot of McKay Street in Maple Ridge, BC. UTM coordinates: 10U 530790m E 5448592m N. The harbour dredge depth goal is -2.5m Chart Datum. 2. McMillan Island Small Craft Harbour is located at the end of Glover Road on the north side of McMillan Island, adjacent to the former Albion Ferry wharf in Langley, BC. UTM coordinates: 10U 531559m E 5447558m N. The harbour dredge depth goal is -3.5m Chart Datum. 3. McIvor’s Landing Small Craft Harbour is located on the south side of the Fraser River, approximately 4 km upstream of the Fort Langley Ferry dock at the foot of 252nd Street, Langley, BC. UTM coordinates: 10U 534615m E 5445688m N. The harbour dredge depth goal is -2.5m Chart Datum. Contractor shall provide all supervision, labour, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, transportation, quality control, health and safety practices, environmental protection, and all other necessary services for the proper and complete execution of the work. Before submitting a bid, bidders can visit the site and its surroundings, at their own expense, to review and verify the form, nature, and extent of the work, materials needed for the completion of the work, the means of access to the site, severity, exposure, and uncertainty of weather, soil conditions, any accommodations they may require, and in general shall obtain all necessary information as to risks, contingencies, and other circumstances which may influence or affect their bid. No allowance shall be made subsequently in this connection on account or error or negligence to properly observe and determine the conditions that will apply. This project must be completed within the work window established by the Fish and Fish Habitat Protection Program (FFHPP) of Fisheries and Oceans Canada, from December 1, 2026, to February 15, 2027, inclusive.

title: Enclosed Trailer
description: Notice of Proposed Procurement The Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) Conservation and Protection Unit has a requirement for a new, enclosed trailer measuring 8.5 feet in width and 28 feet in length. Title: One (1) New, Enclosed Trailer Objective: DFO Conservation and Protection wishes to enter into a contract to acquire one (1) new enclosed trailer measuring 8.5 feet wide and 28 feet long, as per Supply Arrangement E60HP-19TRLR. Scope of Work: The trailer must be equipped as per section 4.0 Requirements of the Supply Arrangement, with the following exceptions/options: 1. Section 5.2 Trailer Front a. The trailer provided must have a flat front (not wedge or V-nose.) 2. Interior Lighting a. The trailer must be provided with interior, ceiling mounted 12 volt lights AND Lights must be provided to illuminate the entire trailer interior to a minimum of 500 lux (lumen/m²) measured with all doors closed. 3. Non-Slip Flooring a. The trailer floor must be provided with a non-slip floor, of a type qualified by the National Floor Safety Institute; b. The Non-Slip material must be permanently affixed to the floor; c. The Non-Slip Material must be of the “Flooring Material” type. Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement: This procurement is no subject to any Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirement: There is no security associated with this requirement. Trade Agreements: The requirement is not subject to any Trade Agreement. The solicitation process is open only to suppliers holding a Supply Arrangement (SA) resulting from Request for Supply Arrangement (RFSA) No. E60HP-19TRLR/A. If you would like to pre-qualify under this RFSA, please click on the following link: RFSA Enclosed Trailers - Tender Notice | CanadaPurchases. Under Offer details, you will be directed to the RFSA.

title: Uudet elintarvikealan kalusteet ja laitteet ammatilliseen koulutukseen
description: HANKINNAN TAUSTAA Koulutuskuntayhtymä OSAOn elintarvikealan koulutus siirtyy Haukiputaan toimipisteeseen osana tilojen uudistamista. Muutoksen yhteydessä rakennetaan ja varustellaan uudet elintarvikealan opetustilat, joihin hankitaan tarjouspyynnön mukaiset keittiölaitteet ja kalusteet. OSAO pyytää tarjouksia laitteista ja kalusteista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. HANKINNAN KOHDE Hankinnan kohteena ovat muun muassa : -keittopadat elintarviketilaan -RST-tasot, hyllyt, tekniikkaseinä -rasvapaistolaite leipomokäyttöön -vaihtolämpökaapit leipomokäyttöön -vesimittari leipomokäyttöön -pikapakastustunnelit elintarvikkeiden ja leipomotuotteiden jäähdytykseen ELINTARVIKEALAN OPETUSTILAT Elintarvikealan perustutkinnon opetusta annetaan kolmella osaamisalalla: elintarviketeknologia, liha-ala ja leipomoala. Elintarvikealan opiskelijat työllistyvät elintarviketeollisuuden työtehtäviin. Tilat toimivat tuotantokeittiöympäristönä, jossa valmistusprosessit ovat teollisen tuotannon kaltaisia ja käsiteltävät tuotantomäärät suuria. Tämän vuoksi laitteiden sijoittelun, mitoituksen ja yhteensopivuuden tulee mahdollistaa sujuva tuotantoprosessi. Tilakokonaisuus sisältää muun muassa seuraavat opetus- ja tuotantoalueet: -Liha- ja kalaosasto, jossa järjestetään liha- ja kala-alan opetusta sekä valmistetaan esimerkiksi makkaroita ja savustettuja tuotteita. -Konditoria- ja jäätelötila, jossa valmistetaan konditoriatuotteita sekä gelatoa. -Leipomo, jossa valmistetaan makeita ja suolaisia leipomotuotteita, kuten ruokaleipää. -Elintarviketilat, joissa suoritetaan elintarvikkeiden esikäsittelyä, valmistusta ja jatkojalostusta. Rakennettavissa opetustiloissa tapahtuu raaka-aineiden säilytys. Tuotantotiloissa tapahtuu raaka-aineiden esikäsittely, valmistus sekä kypsennys. Valmiit tuotteet jäähdytetään jäähdytystunneleissa, jonka jälkeen tuotteet pakataan ja siirretään välivarastoon. Välivarastosta on kuljetus myyntipaikkaan OSAOn Oppipuotiin. TOIMITUS- JA ASENNUSVASTUUT Haukiputaan toimipisteessä toteutetaan kiinteistön muutostyöt, joiden yhteydessä keittiötilat rakennetaan elintarvikealan opetuksen tarpeisiin. Vanhojen keittiölaitteiden ja koneiden purkamisesta sekä niiden uudelleenasennuksesta vastaa pääurakoitsija. Uusien tarjouspyynnön mukaisten laitteiden ja kalusteiden : keittopadat, vaihtolämpökaapit, rasvapaistolaite, pikapakastustunnelit, vesimittari, tekniikkaseinä, tasot, hyllyt ym. kalusteiden toimittamisesta ja asennuksesta vastaa laitetoimittaja yhteistyössä pääurakoitsijan kanssa. Kaikkien keittiölaitteiden ja koneiden lopullisista sähkö-, vesi-, viemäri- ja ilmanvaihtokytkennöistä vastaa pääurakoitsija. Pääurakoitsija vastaa keittiölaitteiden liitosjohdoista ja putkista. TOIMITUSAIKATAULU Toimitusten ja asennusten tulee tapahtua rakennusurakan aikataulun mukaisesti ja yhteistyössä tilaajan sekä pääurakoitsijan kanssa. Laitteet, kalusteet ja osissa toimitettavat pikapakastustunnelit tulee olla toimitettuna ja asennettuna viimeistään viikon 14 aikana, v. 2027. Tekniikkaseinä tulee olla toimitettuna ja asennettuna viimeistään viikolla 9, v.2027. Mikäli pikapakastustunnelit tulevat kokonaisena pakettina, tulee niiden toimitus ja asennus olla viimeistään viikolla 9, v.2027. Tarkemmat toimitusajankohdat sovitaan tilaajan kanssa erikseen. LAITTEIDEN MITOITUS JA YHTEENSOPIVUUS Kalusteiden ja laitteiden tulee vastata tarjouspyynnössä, piirustuksissa ja liiteasiakirjoissa esitettyjä vaatimuksia. Toimittaja vastaa tarjottujen laitteiden ja kalusteiden soveltuvuudesta sekä yhteensopivuudesta asennuspaikkaan. Tiloihin sijoitetaan sekä uusia että nykyisistä tiloista siirrettäviä laitteita ja kalusteita. Koska käytettävissä oleva tila on rajallinen, tarjottavien tuotteiden tule mahtua pohjapiirustuksessa ilmoitettuun paikkaan. Tarjouspyynnön liitteenä oleva Pohjapiirustus (liite 2) on viitteellinen suunnitelma. Osa-alueissa 1 ja 3 tarjoajan tulee liittää tarjouksensa liitteeksi oma keittiölaitesuunnitelma ja tekninen pohjapiirustus, jotka sisältävät kaikki tarjouspyynnön osa-alueissa hankittavat laitteet ja kalusteet. Suunnitelmassa tulee huomioida tilaajan olemassa olevat laitteet ja kalusteet. Suunnitelmissa uusien laitteiden ja kalusteiden tulee muodostaa olemassa olevien laitteiden ja kalusteiden kanssa toimiva ja tarkoituksenmukainen kokonaisuus. Pikapakastustunneleiden (osa-alue 2) osalta tarjoajan tulee liittää tarjouksensa liitteeksi erillinen suunnitelma ja tekninen pohjapiirustus, jossa esitetään mm. tunneleiden mitoitus ja sijoittelu. Näiden tulee olla yhteensopivat samaan tilaan tulevien kylmäsäilytystilojen kanssa, joiden rakentamisesta vastaa urakoitsija. Suunnitelman toimittamatta jättäminen johtaa tarjouksen hylkäämiseen tarjouspyynnön vastaisena. Pohjapiirustukset, kalusteluettelo ja muut tekniset tiedot ovat tarjouspyynnön liitteinä. SOPIMUSKAUSI JA TILAUSMÄÄRÄT Sopimuskausi alkaa, kun hankintasopimus on allekirjoitettu, ja jatkuu siihen saakka, kunnes kaikki sopimuksen mukaiset velvoitteet on asianmukaisesti täytetty. Hankinnalle on varattu määräraha, jonka puitteissa hankinta toteutetaan. Tilausmäärät voivat vaihdella määrärahan puitteissa. SELONOTTONEUVOTTELUT Hankinnasta pidetään ennen hankintapäätöksen tekemistä selonottoneuvottelut. Selonottoneuvottelujen alustava ajankohta on 27.11.2026 ja ne pidetään joko Teamsilla tai osoitteessa Kotkantie 1, Oulu. MARKKINAVUOROPUHELU Hankinnasta on järjestetty markkinavuoropuhelu julkaisemalla kilpailutusmateriaalin luonnos Hilmassa 16.9.2026-30.9.2026 väliseksi ajaksi. Kaikilla kiinnostuneilla toimittajilla on ollut mahdollisuus tutustua materiaaliin ja esittää siihen kommentteja määräaikaan mennessä. Saadut kommentit on huomioitu tarjouspyynnön valmistelussa hankintayksikön harkinnan mukaan., Keittopadat, tekniikkaseinä, RST tasot, hyllyt ja muut kalusteet Osa-alue 1 sisältää: -Uudet keittopadat OSAOn elintarvikealan opetustiloihin. Patoja hankitaan 2kpl ja niiden tulee olla samanlaisia, ns. patapari. Padat ovat pinta-asennettuja, vapaasti seisova malli, ryhmään asennus. LVIS kytkennät tehdään patoihin yhteistyössä pääurakoitsijan kanssa. -Uudet RST-tasot, hyllyt ja tekniikkaseinä OSAOn elintarvikealan opetustiloihin. Urakoitsija tekee kytkennät ja toimittaja tekniikkaseinän kasaamisen/asennuksen., Pikapakastustunnelit elintarvikkeiden ja leipomotuotteiden jäähdytykseen Uudet pikapakastustunnelit, 2kpl, elintarvikkeiden ja leipomotuotteiden jäähdytykseen, OSAOn elintarvikealan opetustiloihin., Rasvapaistolaite, vaihtolämpökaapit ja vesimittari Osa-alue 3 sisältää: -Uuden rasvapaistolaitteen OSAOn leipomon opetustiloihin. -Uudet vaihtolämpökaapit, 2kpl, OSAOn leipomon opetustiloihin. -Uuden vesimittarin OSAOn leipomon opetustiloihin. title: Evaluering av tilskuddsordninger for nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur
description: Kulturdirektoratet forvalter fem tilskuddsordninger for å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk, kultur, identitet og egenorganisering. De nasjonale minoritetene i Norge er kvener/norskfinner, skogfinner, romanifolk/tatere, romer og jøder. Ordningene er sentrale virkemidler for aktiv samfunnsdeltakelse og styrking av språk og kultur. På oppdrag fra Kommunal- og distriktsdepartementet lyser Kulturdirektoratet nå ut en ekstern evaluering av disse ordningene. Formålet med evalueringen er å få kunnskap om hvorvidt, i hvilken grad og på hvilken måte tilskuddsordningene bidrar til å oppfylle målene som er satt og hvordan de eventuelt kan videreutvikles for bedre å styrke nasjonale minoriteters språk og kultur. Oppdragstaker skal vurdere om ordningene er effektive med hensyn til ressursbruk, organisering og måloppnåelse.

title: Poland – Architectural design services – Regulamin konkursu architektoniczno-urbanistycznego na opracowanie koncepcji przebudowy ulic w rejonie Mariensztatu w Warszawie
description: Przedmiotem konkursu jest przebudowa ulic, placów i zieleńców w rejonie Mariensztatu. Przewodnią ideą inwestycji jest uatrakcyjnienie przestrzeni Mariensztatu i jego najbliższego otoczenia. Planowana przebudowa ma posłużyć poprawie jakości i dostępności przestrzeni publicznej oraz ułatwieniu komunikacji pieszej i rowerowej. Zadanie postawione przed uczestnikami konkursu polega na zaproponowaniu przyszłego wizerunku, formy zagospodarowania i sposobu funkcjonowania zespołu ulic, placów i skwerów, które będą stanowiły nowoczesną odpowiedź na aktualne i przyszłe wyzwania dla przestrzeni publicznych na obszarze Historycznego Centrum Warszawy. Teren objęty inwestycją położony jest w Warszawie w obszarze Powiśla i Starego Miasta i obejmuje plac pod wiaduktem pomiędzy ulicami Grodzką i Nowy Zjazd, Rynek Mariensztacki z przylegającymi ulicami: Źródłową, Boczną, Krzywopoboczną, Mariensztat, Garbarska, Białoskórnicza; ul. Sowią z placykiem przy Przedszkolu nr 7, ul. Furmańską. title: Norway – Procurement consultancy services – Procurement assistance for Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency.
description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency has the three main assignments: to procure, administer and phase out material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector. The aim is to give the Norwegian Armed Forces faster reaction ability, higher preparedness and longer perseverance. FMA Procurements are entering into, administering, making call-offs on framework agreements and entering into contracts for/procuring materials in accordance with the law and regulations on public procurements (LOA/FOA/FOSA) as well as internal instructions. The aim of the procurement is to enter into a contract with tenderers who can assist the contracting authority with the implementation of procurements. The assistance shall cover all parts of the procurement process, including planning the preparation of tender documentation, implementation of competition, evaluation of tenders, as well as signing contracts and for individual categories; contract follow-up. See SSA-B annex 1 for further details on the extent of the different categories.

title: Finland – Hotel, restaurant and retail trade services – Mustialan kampuksen matkailupalvelut
description: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulu Oy (HAMK) hakee Mustialan kampukselleen yritystä, joka tuottaa itsenäisesti matkailupalveluja. Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulu tarjoaa toimintaan liittyvät tilat käyttökuluihin nähden edullisella vuokralla, joka on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa. Sopimukseen kuuluu matkailutoiminnan, kuten majoitus-, ohjelma- ja tapahtumapalveluiden tuottamisen, lisäksi mahdollisuus ravintolapalveluiden tarjoamiseen kampuksen panimoravintolassa sekä oluen panemiseen samoissa tiloissa. Sopimus tehdään määräaikaisena ajalle 1.1.2027 - 31.12.2029. Sopimusta on tämän jälkeen mahdollista jatkaa kahden vuoden mittaisella optiojaksolla ajalle 1.1.2030 - 31.12.2031. Option käytöstä sovitaan sopijapuolten kesken yhteisesti. Sopimus on irtisanottavissa kummankin osapuolen toimesta kuuden (6) kuukauden irtisanomisajalla. Hankinta on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.

title: Stage 2 - Sidney Operations Centre Marine Fuel & Docks Replacement, Gulf Islands National Park Reserve
description: Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing docks and marine fueling system at the Sidney Operations Centre (SOC), located at 2220 Harbour Road in Sidney, British Columbia, which serves as the primary Parks Canada Agency office and marine operations base for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The work includes the removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing docks, pilings, and associated servicing systems. The Contractor will supply and install new aluminum-frame docks, pilings, water and electrical services, dock lighting, and a new fueling system consisting of a 5,000-litre fuel tank, fuel lines, and dispenser. All in-water works, including the removal of the existing docks and pilings and the installation of the new docks, must be completed within the lower-risk fisheries window between December 1, 2026, and February 15, 2027. Work occurring above the high-water line may be completed outside of this period. The Contractor will be required to implement the mitigation measures identified in Parks Canada Agency’s Basic Impact Assessment to minimize environmental risks and impacts associated with the project. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: Stage 2 - Lake Annette Retaining Wall Replacement, Jasper National Park
description: REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing retaining wall and reconstruct the adjacent pathway along the Lake Annette Loop Trail in Jasper National Park, Alberta. The project involves the replacement of approximately 110 m of deteriorated retaining wall and the reconstruction of the adjacent 2.0 m wide asphalt pathway located between Lake Annette and Ochre Lake within a high-use day-use area. Construction is anticipated to take place during Fall 2026 to reduce impacts on peak visitor use and take advantage of lower seasonal water levels. The existing natural stone retaining wall has experienced progressive deterioration, resulting in wall instability, pavement cracking, material loss, localized shoreline erosion, and reduced visitor safety. The objective of the project is to restore shoreline stability, improve visitor safety, and provide a durable, low-maintenance infrastructure solution that is compatible with the surrounding natural environment. The Contractor will be responsible for all labour, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the work, including demolition and disposal of the existing retaining wall and pathway, excavation and foundation preparation, installation of a new segmented retaining wall with geogrid reinforcement, reconstruction of the asphalt pathway, drainage improvements, and site clean-up. All work shall be carried out in accordance with the issued engineering drawings, technical specifications, environmental requirements, and contract documents. Revegetation and landscape restoration are not included in this contract and will be solicited separately. Given the environmentally sensitive nature of the site, the Contractor must minimize impacts to adjacent wetlands, shoreline habitat, and visitor-use facilities. Responsibilities will include implementing erosion and sediment control measures, preparing and maintaining an Environmental Protection Plan (EPP), obtaining all required permits, and protecting the work area throughout construction in compliance with Parks Canada environmental requirements. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

Craig United States Army Reserve Center (USARC), located at 915 West Chestnut Street, Brockton, MA 02301-5509. 2. The Government intends to award a single, firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. See Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Clause 52.212-1, "Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Services" and FAR 52.212-1, Addendum for additional information. 5. See FAR Clause 52.212-2, "Evaluation - Commercial Services" and FAR 52.212-2, Addendum for additional information and evaluation criteria. 6. A site visit is not mandatory but is highly recommended. In no event shall failure to inspect the site constitute grounds for a claim after contract award. A Site Visit is available upon request 24 hours prior to the dates listed below. Offerors requesting a site visit shall provide a list of attendees to include the company name, visitor's names, driver's license numbers and state of issues, and vehicle information (make/model/license plate number). Visitors must have a driver's license or state issued ID and proof of auto insurance for entry. The site visit dates and times are as follows: MA006 CPL. Gordon M. Craig USARC 29 October 2026 from 8:30AM to 9:30AM AM EDT ALL VENDORS MUST CONTACT THE BELOW POINT OF CONTACT VIA E-MAIL IF THEY PLAN TO ATTEND. PLEASE PROVIDE WHAT DATE YOU WILL BE ATTENDING. ALL QUESTIONS SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. 7. All questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via Email no later than 2 NOVEMBER 2026 at 10:00 EDT to the Contract Specialist: Mitchell Douglas at mitchell.e.douglas.civ@army.mil and the Contracting Officer: Jasmyne Peterson at jasmyne.c.peterson.civ@army.mil. The questions will be answered all at once and uploaded to the Contract Opportunities website at https://www.sam.gov posting after the question period has ended. 8. All work shall be performed in accordance with Attachment 0001 - Performance Work Statement. 9. All offers shall remain valid for 120 calendar days. 10. COMPLETING A QUOTE FOR SUBMITTAL: a. Quotes shall be posted to the PIEE solicitation website. Offerors that are not posted to this site will be considered non-responsive and shall not be considered for award. b. The Offeror shall provide the name, title, address, email address, and telephone number of the company/division point of contact regarding business decisions made wit respect to the proposal and who can contractually obligate the company. In addition, the contractor shall sign and acknowledge any potential resulting amendments to this solicitation. In doing so, the offeror accedes to the contract terms and conditions as written in the Solicitation. c. The Offeror shall submit a price for each FFP Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) on the Standard Form (SF) 1449 Continuation Sheets of the solicitation. The Government maintains a tax exempt status. d. The offeror shall submit a signed SF1449 (Pg. 1, Block 30a. Signature of Offeror/Contractor). The offeror is required to complete blocks 17, 30a, 30b, and 30c of the SF1449. In doing so, the Offeror accedes to the contract terms and conditions as written in the solicitation. e. Pricing for each CLIN must be submitted in the proper format. The proper format consists of QUANTITY * UNIT PRICE = AMOUNT/NET AMOUNT. In the event there is a discrepancy in the calculation, the UNIT PRICE will be held to the intended price multiplied by the QUANTITY. If the offeror shows only the AMOUNT/NET AMOUNT, but fails to enter a UNIT PRICE, the AMOUNT /NET AMOUNT divided by the QUANTITY will be held to be the intended price. Written Justification must include why this line item is "NSP" and where the price for these services are applied to. description: Centers for Disease Control is issuing this synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for Technical Assistance and Capacity Building for Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity Prevention Strategies. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of acquisition. The possible North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes are 541690 Other Scientific and Technical Consulting Services, size standard of $19 million or 541611 Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services, size standard of $24.5M. There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: organization name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated to deliver technical capability, address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to: provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; implement a successful project management plan that includes compliance with program schedules, cost containment, meeting/tracking performance, hiring/retention of key personnel, and risk mitigation; and provide services under a performance-based service acquisition contract. Based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research and the Government questions attached to this Sources Sought Post, this requirement may be set aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition, and multiple awards may be made. The government will not provide feedback or evaluations to companies regarding their submissions in response to this notice. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response, no more than 3 pages, to include responses to the attachment 0002 Government questions, to this sources sought notice by Tuesday 10 November 2026. All responses under this notice must be emailed to Ann Bonis, won5@cdc.gov. Attachment 0001 DRAFT Performance Work Statement Attachment 0002 Government Questions Technical Assistance

title: What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) Online Study Review Guide (OSRG)

This notice is NOT a request for quotes but is an invitation for potential offerors to express interest and provide information regarding their relevant knowledge, skills, and capabilities. The Department is seeking to gain suitable Market Research for the WWC OSRG. Information submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice may be used to assist the Department in finalizing its acquisition strategy. DISCLAIMER: The Department will not pay for the provision of any information, nor will it compensate any respondents for providing this information. This notice in no way obligates the Government to award any contract to any interested party. Feedback will not be provided to any interested party who submits information to the Department in response to this notice. PLEASE NOTE: All information contained in this notice is preliminary in nature and subject to change. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ), Invitation for Bids (IFB), or a commitment on the part of the Government to conduct a solicitation in the future. All information provided is strictly voluntary and no reimbursement will be made by the Government for any costs associated with providing a response to this notice or otherwise participating in market research activities. Further, the U.S. Department of Education offers no assurance that a solicitation will result from this notice. BACKGROUND: The Institute of Education Sciences (referred to as �the government�) desires a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) alternative to the What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) Online Study Review Guide (OSRG; see �Information About the OSRG� below). The OSRG is a web-based tool that captures data; computes summary statistics; outputs the results of individual study reviews and metanalytic syntheses; and manages workflows associated with government contractors� reviews of academic journal articles against the What Works Clearinghouse standards (see �WWC Standards and Procedures� below). The OSRG is critical to the work of, and is currently maintained by, the government�s WWC contractor (see �Prior Task Order 4 PWS� below). description: Cell Window Glazing This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Kent Institution, Pacific Region. Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: Barring any other conditions or international sanctions, Canadian Suppliers, Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner and Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner, are eligible for this solicitation. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to replace the existing cell window glazing and installation of the polycarbonate security screens to prevent inmates from manipulating window assemblies and receiving contraband delivered by drone. Objectives: To improve the integrity and security of cell windows by installing enhanced glazing and security measures that prevent inmates from damaging, manipulating, removing, or otherwise compromising window assemblies to receive contraband. Deliverables: The Contractor shall: • Supply and install new security glazing in 168 windows located within POD 1 and POD 2, for a total of 504 glazing panels. • Supply and install one polycarbonate security screen on each of the 168 windows in accordance with the construction drawings. • Supply and install all required security screws, fasteners, and accessories identified in the construction drawings and specifications. • Apply security caulking to all newly installed glazing assemblies. • Apply security caulking to the 12 existing windows located in L-Range, POD 1. • Ensure all work is completed in accordance with the construction drawings, specifications, manufacturer’s instructions, and institutional security requirements. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. title: J044--NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Baltimore VAMC Steam System Preventive Maintenance from Vicinity Energy Baltimore Corporation
description: **NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE** This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) RFO 5.101(a) Presolicitation notice requirements and (FAR) RFO 12.102 Restricting Competition. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of an open market sole source award to Vicinity Energy Baltimore Corporation for an annual steam system preventative maintenance contract at the VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS) Baltimore VAMC located at 10 North Greene St. Baltimore, MD 21201. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this service is 561210 (Facilities Support Services). Product Service Code (PSC) is J044 (Maintenance, Repair and Rebuilding of Equipment Furnace, Steam Plant, and Drying Equipment; Nuclear Reactors). Small business size standard is $47.0 Million. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency, by emailing such statement and supporting documentation by NLT 11:00 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST), 11/10/2026 to Contract Specialist Patricia Thai via email at Patricia.Thai@va.gov. Please reference the announcement number (36C24527Q0048) in the subject line of the e-mail. Such documentation will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government under authorities cited above. Statement of Work (SOW) Baltimore VAMC Steam Maintenance Service Contract Introduction: This contract covers all maintenance, repairs, preventive maintenance (PM), and emergency call-back services for the steam system at the Baltimore VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 10 North Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. The Contractor shall perform all services necessary to ensure reliable operation of steam system components and maintain them in accordance with industry standards and manufacturer recommendations. Baltimore VAMC s in-building steam equipment is directly connected to Vicinity Energy s district steam distribution system, which Vicinity owns and operates throughout downtown Baltimore. Because of this interconnected configuration, any work performed on the customer side components can affect not only the Baltimore VAMC but also Vicinity s broader distribution network. No other company owns or operates comparable district steam infrastructure in Baltimore. Therefore, maintenance activities require close coordination with Vicinity s system operations, pressure management, isolation sequencing, and startup/shutdown procedures. Vicinity s technical personnel also maintain proprietary operational data and engineering knowledge that is not readily accessible to third party contractors. A comprehensive preventive maintenance (PM) program would deliver several key benefits: Reliability Reduces outages, operational disruptions, and unexpected system failures Cost Savings Identifies issues early, preventing more costly future repairs Equipment Performance Supports safer, more efficient operation of critical steam dependent systems System Longevity Extends the lifespan and performance of essential steam infrastructure Scope of Services: The Contractor shall provide a two-person crew for eight (8) hours every two weeks (totaling 416 labor hours per year) to maintain steam system components, including: Performing steam trap surveys Cleaning pressure-reducing valves Inspecting heat exchangers and steam converters Ensuring proper operation of condensate tanks, pumps, and piping Identifying and addressing steam piping or valve leaks Verifying proper operation of all meters Ensuring proper water chemistry Assisting with regulatory inspections Parts and Materials: The Contractor shall supply all parts, materials, equipment, and tools necessary to complete the work described. All replacement parts shall meet the original manufacturer s specifications or be approved equivalents. Emergency Service: The Contractor shall provide prompt emergency call-back service within five (5) hours of notification by the Contracting Officer (CO), Contracting Officer s Representative (COR), or their designees. A qualified service technician must be on site within five (5) hours when emergency repairs are required due to system shutdowns or critical issues arising between scheduled service visits. Service Reporting: Upon completion of each PM service, the Contractor shall submit a written report to the COR detailing the services performed, corrective actions taken, parts used, and recommendations for extending the useful life of steam system components. General Information, Requirements and Expectations: The Contractor shall check in with the Plumbing Shop or Utility Systems Repairer Operator (USRO) Supervisors upon arrival at the facility. An emergency telephone number must be provided for urgent repair needs. Contractor personnel are required to wear uniforms that display the company name in a clear and permanent manner for easy identification. Tour of Duty: All routine work will be performed during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, except in cases of emergency call-back. Routine maintenance should not be scheduled on observed Federal Holidays. Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is one (1) year from the contract award date, with potential option-year periods to be exercised at the Government s discretion. Place of Performance: All work shall be performed at Baltimore VA Medical Center (VAMC) 10 North Greene Street, Baltimore, MD 21201. Security, Safety, and Access Requirements: Contractor personnel shall follow all VA security, safety, and infection control requirements. Contractor vehicles, tools, and equipment may be subject to inspection. The Contractor shall ensure adherence to all facility safety policies and immediately report unsafe conditions to the COR.

title: DNWP0027- Lot 1B / WAGR B55 Demolition - Sellafield - A2R JV
description: The B55 and B55.2 demolition project at Sellafield involves the controlled demolition and dismantling of the B55 Office Complex and B55.2 Turbine Hall, located within the WAGR complex, down to existing ground-floor slab level. The scope includes soft stripping, asbestos remediation, high-reach mechanical demolition of the structural frame, cladding and reinforced-concrete floors, together with segregation and processing of demolition arisings, backfilling of voids and final site clearance. A key constraint is Substation 65, which is located within the B55/B55.2 structure and must remain operational and be protected from demolition impacts, dust and water ingress throughout the works. Retained basements and associated structures also require protection, while uncertainties associated with ageing structures, buried services, below-ground voids and incomplete historical information must be managed through robust surveys, demolition engineering and risk-informed planning. Overall, the project is intended to provide a safe, demolition-led solution that reduces workforce exposure, removes redundant infrastructure and supports accelerated hazard reduction across the wider WAGR decommissioning programme. Additional information: https://www.linkedin.com/company/a2r-altrad-atkinsrealis-remediation https://www.gov.uk/government/news/sellafield-ltd-awards-high-hazard-risk-reduction-framework-contract

title: Facility Investment Services for Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point North Carolina and outlying fields Bogue, Atlantic, BT 11 and BT 9
description: This is not a request for either a quote or proposal, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potential offerors of a Performance-Based Facility Support Service Type Contract, with Recurring and Non-Recurring Services at Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. The contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment required to perform Facility Investment Services for facilities, ground structures, and installed equipment and systems at Marine Corp Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point North Carolina and outlying fields Bogue, Atlantic, BT 11 and BT 9. BT 11 and BT 9 are islands located in the Pamlico Sound, which is accessible only by boat. General Work Requirements: The contractor shall provide facility support services that include, but are not limited to: Service Orders / Ticket Work HVAC Water Testing and Treatment Services Boilers and Unfired Pressure Vessels Boiler Plant Controls Boiler Water Testing and Treatment Services Fire Protection Systems, Fire Suppression, CO2 Fire Suppression Systems Gaylord/Ansul Hoods and Ducts Systems Vertical Transportation Equipment (VTE) Medical Gas Delivery System AV8B Engine Test Cell Annual Cleaning of Hangar Floors Actuator Valves Paint Stripping Booth Equipment Reverse Osmosis Ultra-Violet System Compressed Air Systems Atlas Copco United Blowers Positive Displacement Maintenance Scale Calibration Turnstile and Gate Maintenance Flow Meter Calibration Tool Calibration, including high voltage tools Inspection of Elevated Potable Water Tanks Cathodic Protection Systems Certification and Calibration of Parshall Flumes Calibration, Certification, and Servicing HACH Probes Analyzers and Sensors Calibration, and Certification Gas Monitoring System IWTP B-4380 VTE Certification Support Grease Traps Sewage Plant Sludge Removal and Land Application Alkaline Stabilizing and Stabilized Liquid Sludge Port-A-John Service Sealed Vault Toilet/Septic Tanks Pond Maintenance Aquatic Weed Fisheries Management Source selection procedures will be used to select the best value offeror using tradeoff analysis in accordance with FAR Part 15 � Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the request for proposal (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Management Approach, Factor 2 � Recent, Relevant Experience of the Firm, Factor 3 � Safety, and Factor 4 � Past Performance. The proposed procurement will be issued as an indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) type contract with recurring and non-recurring services. The IDIQ contract will include online ordering capability using FedMall for the non-recurring exhibit line item numbers (ELINs). Acceptance of Government Purchase Credit Cards is required along with the purchase of FedMall encrypted software. The North American Classification System (NAICS) is 561210; the size standard is $47M. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period of one year with four (4) one-year option periods, which, cumulatively, will not exceed (60) months. This contract will include a phase-in period. If the Government does not award a follow-on contract in time, the Government may require the Contractor to continue performance for an additional period up to six months under the Option to Extend Services clause. A sources sought notice N4008526R0042 for this procurement was posted on 5 December 2025 on SAM, and a market survey was conducted that included an assessment of relevant qualifications and capabilities of potentially qualified firms. As a result of the market research analysis, a determination was made to set aside this procurement under the Small Business Program. The NAVFAC MIDLANT small business office, as well as the Small Business Association, concurs with this decision. The proposed procurement will be listed as a competitive 100 percent small business set-aside. The Government will only accept offers from small business concerns. The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be made available in electronic format only (Adobe Acrobat (pdf)) and will be posted on SAM.gov website on or about 12 November 2026. The estimated proposal due date shall be at least 30 days after the RFP is posted. All prospective contractors are required to register on the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the Internet at https://sam.gov/. Notifications of any updates or amendments to the solicitation will be posted on the SAM. Only registered contractors will be notified by e-mail when amendments to the solicitation are issued. description: Solicitation Notice: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Commercial Lodging BPA (FA301627Q0008)Scope of Work The 502d Contracting Squadron (502 CONS CL) at JBSA Lackland, Texas, is soliciting quotes to establish up to six (6) decentralized, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for commercial off-base lodging accommodations. title: Canned Fruit for use in Domestic Food Assistance Programs
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 5.101(d). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 2000011585 is issued as a IFB for Canned Fruit. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source � NSA Annapolis, Maryland UESC
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) intends to award a Utility Energy Service Contract (UESC) to Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) for the design, construction, commissioning, and financing of a comprehensive energy resilience project at Naval Support Activity (NSA) Annapolis, Maryland. The proposed project, estimated at approximately $45 million, will include a Combined Heat and Power (CHP) cogeneration plant integrated with a microgrid to enhance installation energy resilience. Major project elements include: A CHP system supporting an estimated 19 MW peak electrical demand, including three natural gas-fired turbines and associated heat-recovery systems; An integrated microgrid control system capable of island-mode operation during utility grid outages; An absorption chiller at the Lejeune Chilled Water Plant (597U) utilizing recovered waste heat; Relocation and upgrade of the 13C-1 electrical substation; Required natural-gas infrastructure upgrades and electric-grid interconnection activities; An Investment Grade Audit (IGA), design, engineering, construction, testing, commissioning, and construction management; and Operator training and project turnover documentation. Basis for Intended Sole Source The Government intends to use other than full and open competition pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) and FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The proposed action will be implemented as a UESC pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2913(d). BGE is the franchised electric and natural-gas utility serving NSA Annapolis and owns and operates the affected utility distribution infrastructure. GSA Areawide Public Utility Contract No. 47PA0724D0003 provides for BGE electric, natural-gas, and energy-management services within its franchised service territory. The contemplated UESC requires integrated responsibility for natural-gas capacity upgrades, electric-system interconnection, grid coordination, and modifications affecting BGE-owned or controlled infrastructure. These functions are integral to the CHP, microgrid, and island-mode requirements. The Government issued a Sources Sought Notice on February 5, 2026, which closed on February 20, 2026. Five firms responded to the notice. Based on the Government�s market research, acquisition planning, and review of the responses received, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) was determined to be the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirements. BGE was the only respondent possessing the requisite utility-service authority, control of the affected infrastructure, and ability to execute or authorize the necessary utility-system modifications and interconnection activities required to perform the contemplated UESC. Submission of Capability Information This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, responsible sources that believe they possess the capability, legal authority, and financing capacity to perform the complete requirement may submit a written capability statement. Capability statements should demonstrate: Legal authorization to provide the required electric and natural-gas utility services to NSA Annapolis; Authority and ability to execute or authorize the required utility-infrastructure modifications; Ability to perform and coordinate required electric-grid interconnection activities, including coordination with PJM Interconnection and applicable stakeholders; Experience with projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity under a UESC or comparable utility-financed arrangement; and Ability to provide the financing necessary to implement the project. Responses shall contain sufficient information for the Government to determine whether the respondent can satisfy the complete requirement and shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to olisha.g.costa.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 1:00 PM Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The Government will consider timely responses before determining whether to proceed with the contemplated sole-source action. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this notice.

title: Automated Fluidized Bed Mixer Facility Modernization for end use at Pine Bluff Arsenal � CSO
description: The purpose of this Commercial Solution Opportunity (CSO) is to seek out qualified vendors who have experience manufacturing an Automated Fluidized Bed Mixer Facility Modernization for end use at Pine Bluff Arsenal. This announcement is in support of market research performed by the Army Contract Command - Rock Island to determine interest and capability to provide the supply defined within this CSO. This CSO will utilize a solicitation process authorized by RFO DFARS 212.70. Under this CSO, the DoW will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial items, technologies, and services. CSO procedures provide a streamlined acquisition process and simplified contract terms resulting in FAR-based contracts awarded under Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures. Both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors may be awarded contracts under this CSO. Under a CSO DoW contracting officers may competitively select quotes received in response to a general competitive solicitation, similar to a broad agency announcement, based on a review of quotes by scientific, technological, or other subject matter experts. Please provide your Reponses to the following questions below through email to Ashley Testake, ashley.e.testrake.civ@mail.mil NLT COB 14 October 2026.

description: 36C25527R0013 Pre-solicitation Notice Pre-Solicitation Notice: Request for Architectural and Engineer SF330 Submission for Solicitation: 36C25527R0013, Replace Medium Voltage Feeder 3 and Transformers, Project No. 657A5-24-108. CONTRACT INFORMATION This A-E Services requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law (PL0582) and implemented in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 36.102. Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work. This procurement is restricted to Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. This is not a Request for Proposal, and an award will not be made with this announcement. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR) HQ, in support of the Program Executive Office (PEO) Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C41) International Integration Program Office (PMW 740) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) N0003926RE014 to procure Autonomous INTelligence System (AINTS) platforms and capabilities to enhance the operational system and mission for the Egyptian Navy (EN) per Foreign Military Sales (FMS) case EG-P-LGQ. This contract will include Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for labor, Cost-Reimbursement, non-fee bearing CLINs for travel/other direct costs (ODCs), and Firm-Fixed-Price CLINs for Material/Equipment/Spares. Any information submitted in response to this RFP will become property of the U.S. Government. All questions/comments are to be submitted in writing to Ms. Kristin White, Contracting Officer, at kristin.l.white4.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Kimberly Ellis, Contracts Specialist, at kimberly.a.ellis10.civ@us.navy.mil. The specific requirements for this RFP will include Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be made publicly available. If an Offeror has previously submitted an NDA for this procurement, a new NDA will not need to be re-submitted unless there are changes to the previous submission. Only one NDA per Company (Prime/Sub) is required at this time. Note: Please make sure your cage code is included and all sections of the NDA is completed in order to not cause a delay in receiving access. Currently the CUI Limited Dissemination Control List only allows for Department of Defense (DoD) and U.S. DoD Contractors only. Interested parties should submit the attached NDA to Kristin White at kristin.l.white4.civ@us.navy.mil and Kimberly Ellis at kimberly.a.ellis10.civ@us.navy.mil.
